texto_ingles:
{span 14 9c4b 22 20}  High champion of the Dark Knights Loslorien.
  He was sent to Valeria when a secret treaty was forged between the Holy Lodissian Empire and the Bakram leader Brantyn. However, his true task was to occupy Valeria and seek the wondrous powers thought hidden there.
  He attempted to use the sword Brynhildr stolen from the Kingdom of New Xenobia to unravel the mystery of these powers. However, finally realizing they were beyond man's control, he considered withdrawing from Valeria.
  He was detained when Sir Martym and Sir Barbas rebelled against him, but later escaped during a battle between Resistance and Bakram forces. His current whereabouts are not known.

texto_ingles:
{span 12 7c47 37 18}  A Loslorien commander from Galius, seat of the Holy Lodissian Empire.
  He is known for his cunning swordplay. He will stop at nothing to achieve victory, living by the motto, "It always comes to blood." Though his words lack grace, he wields a blade with great finesse.
  He was one of the Dark Knights who attacked Golyat. Together with Sir Barbas he also took part in the sacking of Rhime, where he clashed steel with Sir Gildas.

{span 12 4047 29 20}  A Loslorien commander hailing from Bomouth on the borderlands of Lodis.
  He is a giant of a man, and the most bloodthirsty of the seven Loslorien commanders. He was put on trial for beating a superior to death, but was saved from execution by Lanselot Tartaros.
  He led the Bakram forces invading Rhime, and battled the Holy Knight Lanselot there. He was also among the Dark Knights who attacked Golyat a year ago.

texto_ingles:
{span 1c aa49 1e 18}  A Loslorien commander from Galius, seat of the Holy Lodissian Empire, and twin brother to Dame Ozma.
  He is an expert swordsman, receiving top honors from the Xanam Officer's Academy. After serving as commander of three regiments of the Ganan Division for a number of years, he was assigned to the Dark Knights.   Ordered by Lanselot Tartaros to finish off remaining partisan forces, he headed to Boed Fortress with Dame Ozma.

texto_ingles:
{span 2c 844b 07 10}  A Bakram who serves as regent to the Bakram-Valerian Kingdom. Following the death of King Dorgalua, he aspired to rule Valeria himself.
  Though once a mere abuna in the Order of Philaha, he used his growing power in the church to intervene in the power struggle caused by the lack of a successor. He consolidated his political power by courting the favor of the noble and wealthy. Backed by the military might of Lodis to the north, he established the Bakram-Valerian Kingdom and installed himself as regent. The kingdom is headed by the heir of House Eltynaha due to their blood ties with Queen Vernotta, but it is Brantyn who rules.

texto_ingles:
{span 39 024f 2d 18 0c7230313030}  A Bakram who once served as regent to the Bakram-Valerian Kingdom. He was brother to Abuna Prancet, and the uncle of {hero}.
  Though once a mere abuna of the Order of Philaha, after the king's death he shared his knowledge of Catiua with the queen to curry favor, and attained the rank of exarch. He then exploited his position to intervene in the power struggle caused by the lack of a successor. He consolidated his political power through the support of the noble and wealthy classes. Backed by the military might of Lodis to the north, he established the Bakram-Valerian Kingdom and installed himself as regent. The kingdom was headed by the heir of House Eltynaha due to their blood ties with Queen Vernotta, but Brantyn ruled from the shadows.
  Brantyn was ordered to make peace with the Resistance when Princess Versalia's existence came to light, but he would not relent. He died fighting Resistance forces at Heim Castle.

{span 27 2849 24 10 0c4430313030}  A Galgastani who served her clan in battle. texto_ingles:
{span 27 ca4d 1e 18 0a9e30313030}  A Bakram who is wed to the pirate Darza. She was born to nobility in Barnicia, but struck out on her own to escape the burden of her lineage. While at sea her ship was attacked by Darza's pirates, and she was taken to Ndamsa Fortress. She was unfazed by their threats of violence, and Darza grew fond of her spirited nature, keeping her always at his side. Veldrei eventually came to have feelings for Darza as well, and they married.
  At first she joined him on raids, but later stayed ashore to watch over their den after learning she carried Darza's child. Though usually calm and collected in front of the other pirates, she broke into tears upon hearing of Darza's death.
  She was defeated in battle by {hero} while attempting to avenge her husband's killing, but her life was spared.

texto_ingles:
{span 25 944b 0d 18 0a7c30313030}  A Galgastani who served his clan in battle. He was the son of renowned architect Selba Brondel. Selba created many famed buildings, such as Heilingham Palace, also known as the Hanging Gardens. Orba taught at the Coritanae Academy of Arts while painting numerous works in his spare time. One of these, named "Opalescent Clouds," was presented to the late King Dorgalua, and now hangs in Heim Castle.
  Orba was a major proponent of the nationalism espoused by Hierophant Balbatos, and he volunteered to take up arms soon after war broke out.
  He encountered Resistance forces at Tynemouth while en route to Almorica, and was slain by {hero} Pavel.

texto_ingles:
{span 1f 784c 3d 18 104830323030}  A Walister who served the New Walister Alliance. Gousin wanted to fight for his people, but his poor upbringing led to him resenting nobility, and he was hesitant to join the Resistance with Duke Ronwey at the helm. He later learned that the New Walister Alliance also sought self-governance for the Walister, and resolved to join them.
  Gousin was a devout follower of the Order of Philaha, which preaches that all are equal in the eyes of the Great Father. He prayed before each battle and at dusk each day, earning him the moniker "Gousin the Devout" among his fellow soldiers.
  While en route to Almorica to rally like-minded soldiers to the cause, he was killed by {hero} on the Golborza Plain. It seemed he had heard a great deal of {hero}'s sister, Catiua.

{span 2f 184c 3c 18 0f7e30313030 0a7e30313030}  A Galgastani who served his clan in battle. He was the son of renowned architect Selba Brondel. His twin brother Orba was slain by {hero} at Tynemouth.
  Garba had won fame as a political philosopher, penning works such as "The Creed of the Self-Deceived" and "Failings of Present-Day Doctrine." Though initially an advocate of progressive politics, he took a more nationalistic tone after hearing the words of Hierophant Balbatos. He stated in one address, "Nothing can assuage the resentment we harbor toward the Walister, though we may know it unjust." The way he calmly vanquished his opponents in argument earned him the name "Garba the Silver-Tongued."
  He was slain by {hero} Pavel on the Xeod Moors while marching to engage Resistance forces at Balmamusa.

texto_ingles:
{span 27 6e4e 0f 18 06d030313030}  A Galgastani who served his clan in battle. During the reign of King Dorgalua, deadly swordfights were a popular form of entertainment among wealthy Bakram in Heim. Only gladiators were permitted to participate in these bouts to the death. These gladiators were deserters or criminals chosen for their fighting ability. By choosing the path of the gladiator they escaped execution and were granted a small chance of freedom.
  Brezen was once a gladiator himself, surviving numerous bouts to eventually win his liberty. His skill in battle saw him recruited into the army, but he was disliked by others for his vulgar manners. He was bullied mercilessly and made the target of much unjustified scorn. texto_ingles:
{span 25 244c 30 18 0c7830313030}  A Walister who once served with the Walister Resistance. She was a spiritualist at the village of Vanan near the border of Almorica, contacting the dead to pass on messages to their kin. Regardless of whether her talents were genuine, Ramidos brought peace to many grieving loved ones. Her father died at an early age, and it is clear that her mother instilled in her a strong sense of compassion.
  She lived in Vanan with her son's family, but all her kin were slain when the village was sacked in the early days of the war. She then joined the Walister Resistance as a spellbinder, specializing in offensive magic.
  She was killed in battle when {hero} arrived at Almorica Castle to free Catiua, who had been kidnapped by Xapan the Mercenary.

{span 23 464b 22 18 06d230313030}  A Galgastani who served her clan in battle. House Apollinaire is a noble family related to former Lord of Coritanae, Count Orlandeau. For generations they have held seats in the House of Nobles, wielding great power throughout the region. Daesi Apollinaire, youngest daughter of the current family head, favored warfare over politics, eventually attaining the rank of commander.

  She died attempting to fend off {hero}'s assault on Coritanae Keep.

{span 18 a849 04 18}  A Galgastani who once fought for the armies of Galgastan.
  She was a necromancer who tampered with the souls of the dead. She studied under the Necromancer Nybeth together with her daughters Moldova and Cressida. They believed that necromancy allowed those who died before their time a chance to fulfill their ambitions.
  Cassandra battled Resistance forces to avenge her daughter Moldova's killing, but was defeated. Nybeth had given her a means to avoid death, but there was no effect, and she perished.
